newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end higher after jittery trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares end higher after jittery trade.

text.p: Germany's IBIS DAX index of German shares ended the day in positive territory on Wednesday, but the prospect of further gains this week was ruled out by a market rendered jittery after a long period of record highs.

"It's not particularly hectic out there at the moment, but then these are nervous times. We've got a meeting of the Federal Reserve next week and the British elections coming up to make everyone jittery," a trader said.
The 30-share IBIS DAX index ended electronic trade at 3,305.72 points, up 16.13 points or 0.49 percent, while DTB DAX futures were up 13.5 points at 3,309 points.
"The triple-witching later this week also makes the market very superficial and any gains tend to be based on movements in derivatives," the trader said.

Traders said that weaker performances on Wall Street were also dampening sentiment, but said the current slow-down or correction was "not unhealthy". "People will pick up stocks on the way down," a trader said.
Among shares in the news was the engineering group Preussag AG, which ended up 18 marks at 459.80 marks, as merger mania in the steel/engineering group lifted the share 4.07 percent.
Focus has centred on the steel industry since Fried. Krupp AG's launched a 13.6 billion mark takeover for Thyssen AG.

Since then Krupp has proposed cooperation talks with Thyssen. The news also boosted Mannesmann AG, which ended up 18.50 marks at 641.50 marks. A slightly weaker dollar at 1.68 marks also impacted on sentiment.

Shares in German drugs group Schering rose initially after it revised its sales and profits forecasts for 1997, fell amid afternoon profit taking, but re-emerged to end the day up 5.20 marks at 162.30 marks.
